newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan hotel privatization delayed one week.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan hotel privatization delayed one week.

text.p: The auction of Venezuela's five-star, half-finished and state-owned Hotel Melia has been postponed for one week, until November 22, at the request of two potential bidders, officials said.
"They asked for an extension saying they hadn't had time to gather all the funds required," said an official of Banco Industrial de Venezuela (BIV), which owns the building.
It is the second time this year that the planned auction of the hotel complex in central Caracas has been postponed.
The two interested bidders are U.S. group Entertainment Resorts Development Int. and CSL Credito Subalpino di Lugano of Switzerland, BIV official Roberto Piol said on Thursday.
The base price has been fixed at 15.4 billion bolivars ($33 million) for the 624-room hotel, which includes a large commercial center, a swimming pool and a heliport.

Construction of what is potentially one of the largest and most luxurious hotel complexes in Latin America, according to the BIV, began in 1987. It was stopped in early 1994 when the then- owner could not meet bank payments and the property was transferred to the BIV.
